title: Add API-contract fallback adapter + Beta-Contract header for streaming, tools, and structured outputs
author: Maya Liang
release_notes: Introduce a non-breaking runtime adapter and an opt-in Beta-Contract header to allow clients to exercise a new API contract for streaming, tool/function calling, and structured outputs. Existing clients unchanged unless they opt in.
body:
Motivation: We are rolling out a tightened API contract that clarifies streaming chunk semantics, deterministic tool/function-calling payloads, and a more explicit structured-output framing. To avoid breaking existing customers and to enable staged opt-in, this PR introduces a runtime "fallback adapter" and an opt-in request header (Beta-Contract) that toggles the new contract behavior for a single request. The goal is to let client SDKs and downstream services validate the new contract in production traffic without forcing a global server-side switch.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a lightweight adapter layer in the OpenAI-compatibility route that performs request/response normalization when Beta-Contract is present. The adapter enforces stricter streaming delimiters, canonicalizes function-call payloads, and validates structured-output envelopes.
- Implements a Beta-Contract request header: "X-Redwood-Beta-Contract: v1-preview". Header is ignored for older clients. The header enables the adapter path and is logged for telemetry.
- Ensures streaming stability by adding an idempotent chunk reassembly pass that handles corner cases where partial delta tokens previously caused malformed JSON in structured outputs. This includes a backoff/retry for the streaming parser when it encounters non-terminal tokens.
- Provides compatibility hooks in the tool/function-calling layer so that invocation targets receive the canonicalized args shape (array-of-objects canonicalization) while still preserving original metadata in a "compat_meta" field for debugging.
- Adds a comprehensive test matrix (unit + integration) that asserts parity for legacy traffic and verifies contract behavior with Beta-Contract header enabled.

Commits (summary):
- 3a7b4c1: feat(adapter): add runtime fallback adapter and header parsing; basic telemetry events
- b8d9f02: fix(stream): robust chunk reassembly and streaming parser retry; add parser metrics
- c44211e: feat(tools): canonicalize function-call args and attach compat_meta; update tool runtime contract tests
- e1f90a6: test(ci): add integration matrix for old vs beta contract; include synthetic streaming edgecases
- f7550d3: docs: add header spec and migration guidance to openai-compat README

Changed files (high level):
- src/compat/adapter/fallback_adapter.py (new) - adapter implementation and header hook
- src/compat/middleware/header_middleware.py (mod) - parse and validate Beta-Contract header
- src/compat/streaming/parser.py (mod) - idempotent reassembly, retry logic, metrics hooks
- src/compat/tools/canonicalizer.py (new) - function-call args canonicalization + compat_meta
- tests/compat/test_beta_contract_matrix.py (new) - matrix test harness
- docs/openai-compat/contract-beta.md (new) - header spec, examples, telemetry notes
- ci/pipelines/compat-matrix.yml (mod) - run integration matrix in PR CI
- examples/compat-demo/client_preview.py (new) - sample client showing header usage

Notes on backward compatibility: The adapter is strictly opt-in. No change to default runtime for existing requests. The header is intentionally verbose to discourage accidental rollouts. Existing SDKs will continue to work; SDK maintainers can ship an opt-in toggle that sets the header during beta trials. There is an "adapter-telemetry" event that surfaces when a request uses the Beta-Contract and when the adapter falls back to legacy normalization due to an unparseable stream chunk.

Review conversation (selected excerpts):
- Ethan Cole (reviewer): "This looks good overall. Two asks: 1) add a small benchmark to measure adapter overhead in p95 for short requests, 2) ensure the compat_meta does not leak sensitive user data by default."
- Maya Liang (author): "Added the micro-benchmark; compat_meta is gated behind a debug flag and redacted by default. See tests and README notes."
- Rosa Alvarez (reviewer): "Streaming reassembly is the right call. Could we avoid introducing additional cross-process retries? I'm worried about head-of-line blocking in battched serving lanes."
- Daniel Kim (reviewer): "Confirmed CI matrix passed on my re-run. Verified the adapter adds ~1.8ms p95 on short text-gen requests in our lab; acceptable for beta trials."

CI summary: The PR runs the compat integration matrix (old vs beta), unit tests, packaging, lint, and the streaming-legitimacy suite. The first CI run had a flaky test in tests/streaming/test_fragmented_json.py which was fixed by increasing the parser buffer threshold; final CI status: all checks passed.

Operational considerations:
- Telemetry: new events: compat.adapter.used, compat.adapter.fallback, compat.parser.retry, compat.header.invalid. These are available in Console with a 24h default retention for the beta.
- Rollout plan: Beta usage is controlled client-side. After a two-week opt-in period and no regressions reported by the QA channel, we'll consider enabling a rolling opt-in for internal SDKs and feature flags. No forceful server-side flip is planned in this PR.
- Observability: Added dashboards for parser retry rates and adapter p95 cost. Alerting threshold suggested at 5% retry rate over 15m.

Merge decision: After reviews and CI green, PR was squashed and merged to main. No migration script required.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-2179: Add server-side feature-flag to apply adapter per-customer for controlled experiments (not included in this PR).
- PM-649: Draft customer-facing migration notes and SDK opt-in snippets for the next docs push.

This PR is intentionally conservative: it provides a path to test the new contract without breaking traffic and gives engineers a way to debug contract regressions with compat_meta and telemetry. The implementation emphasizes minimal latency overhead and explicit opt-in semantics.
